title: Output format violation injection and remediation runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Runbook and test plan to intentionally inject output-format violations into streaming and tool-call scenarios, validate detection and automated remediation flows, and measure regression risk for constrained-decoding enforcement. The aim is to exercise partial-stream interruptions, interleaved tool outputs, adversarial token sequences, and model fallback behaviors to ensure API consumers observe predictable, reparable failures or graceful degradation.
background: We have recurring edge cases where enforced output formats (e.g., JSON-mode) are violated during streaming or when tool calls interleave with structured payloads. Existing tests cover canonical compliance but insufficiently probe adversarial injection vectors, partial emits, and cross-model compatibility when an enforced schema changes. This ticket consolidates an injection harness, observability metrics, and remediation runbook for on-call and CI automation.
scope: Create an adversarial injection harness for streaming and function-calling paths, add detectors for format violations upstream in the gateway, implement an automated remediation path (canonicalization + tolerant-decoder fallback), and add CI canaries that run the harness against recent model versions and quantization profiles.
out_of_scope: Changes to model training or upstream tokenizer behavior. Major runtime kernel rewrites. Full migration of all legacy SDKs (we will add compatibility smoke checks only).
success_criteria: Injection harness covers at least 12 distinct violation patterns (partial JSON, extra commas, truncated arrays, interleaved tool-return tokens, rogue function call tokens)
Gateway detectors flag violations with <1% false positive rate on production sample traffic (measured over a 24h window)
Automated remediation flow reduces customer-facing error rate for constrained-decoding failures by >=70% in canary traffic
CI canary runs on every model onboarding and blocks merges with high regression signals
test_plan: Design 12 injection scenarios and map to streaming+toolcall combinations
Implement harness in tests/structured-output/adversarial_harness.py (runs against runtime canary endpoint)
Add gateway detector that inspects token stream boundaries and validates incremental parseability
Create tolerant-decoder service that attempts progressive repairs: close-open brackets, canonicalizer passes, then fallback to constrained decode with relaxed schema
Integrate remediation flow as optional automatic response for canary routes and as a manual runbook for production incidents
Add CI job 'str-output-injector' that runs harness against model bundles in PRs and fails if high violation regressions detected
injection_scenarios: Partial stream termination mid-object (e.g., truncated JSON after key)
Interleaved toolcall JSON payload inserted between top-level keys
Adversarial token like '\u0000' or long delimiter sequences inside string values
Duplicate closing braces and trailing garbage tokens
Streaming rate-limiter induced chunk split inside UTF-8 multibyte char
Model switch mid-response (fallback to smaller variant) that alters output shape
Quantized model artifact producing misordered token sequences
Injected commentary or hallucinated schema field name changes
Function-call token emitted before structured payload completed
Array items partially emitted with trailing ellipsis tokens
Unexpected sentinel tokens from older SDKs embedded in stream
Ambiguous delimiter tokens from multi-language prompts
observability_and_metrics: Alert: violation_rate > 0.5% for 15m on production routes (pager)
Dashboards: per-model heatmap of violation types and remediation success
Trace: sample full request/response stream with redaction for PII
remediation_flow: Detect incremental parse failure at gateway streaming parser
Attempt in-flight canonicalizer that closes minimal number of brackets or removes trailing garbage
If canonicalizer succeeds, return repaired payload to client with 'x-structured-output-repaired: true' header
If canonicalizer fails, run tolerant-decoder fallback with relaxed schema and add 'x-structured-output-fallback: tolerant' header
Record remediation outcome to violation.events and increment remediation.rate metric
If both fail and route is high-priority customer, trigger on-call runbook with sample artifact
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge harness and gateway detector behind feature flag; run nightly canaries against staging
Stage 2: Enable automatic canonicalizer for internal canary routes only; monitor metrics for 72h
Stage 3: Expand to 10% production traffic for low-risk routes; keep automatic remediation off for enterprise customer routes unless opt-in
Stage 4: Full rollout with opt-out by customer for sensitive workloads
Rollback: disable canonicalizer flag and disable CI gate if remediation causes regressions
runbook_steps: On alert, capture last 10s of streaming tokens and save to /tmp/str-violation-<id>.log
If repair succeeds, note incident as 'auto-repaired' and notify customer success
If repair fails, escalate to on-call runtime engineer and attach model bundle and quantization profile
Open a follow-up ticket if violation correlated with model version or recent deployment
notes: This ticket intentionally targets behavior-level mitigation rather than deeper model fixes to provide a safety net for customers while model and tokenizer teams investigate recurrent violations. Aim for measurable reduction in customer-facing errors and clear signals for future model onboarding hardening.
